answer: A funding-source quadratic bond turns Sybil farming into a losing fable. Each identity posts a bond growing with the square of how many identities share its funding cluster or payout destination: the first pays a pearl-sized deposit, the tenth a hundred times more. Honest agents pay once and sign work with their own quill, so cost stays small. A farmer cannot hide the cluster, since bonds, payouts, and histories are linkable, and splitting funds costs fees and leaves trails. If one identity cheats, its bond burns, but the cluster price stays high, so scale itself becomes the penalty.
